subject: Post-call: deployment mode qualification & pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: John Park <john@velox.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: deployment mode qualification & next steps

Hi John —

Great to talk earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use: real-time customer chat (low-latency text generation) with occasional batch embedding jobs for search.
- Current volume estimate: ~10M text-generation requests / month (avg prompt+response ~250 tokens).
- Latency SLO: 95th <200ms for UI interactions.
- Data residency: US only for now, possible future EU requirement.
- Compliance: standard SOC 2 required; may need stricter logging/audit for 2027.

Initial deployment mode lean
- Hosted API: fastest to ship; per-token economics likely appealing for lower commits, but hard to guarantee 95th <200ms at 10M reqs without burst capacity.
- Dedicated: recommended if you want predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale (reserved GPU pools + burst).
- Private VPC/on-prem: only needed if you must keep control of Networking/KMS or air-gapped.

Requested from your side
- Confirm concurrency peaks (RPS) and any sustained throughput windows.
- Confirm whether embeddings will run on same SLA/low-latency path or can be async.

Next steps
1) I’ll put together a high-level cost model for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (reserved commit examples + per-token comparisons). Attached a quick requirements workbook — fill any missing numbers.
2) We’ll loop in Marissa for Dedicated sizing and Neha for pricing approvals if the numbers point that way.
3) Schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to review model and recommend a deployment plan.

Thanks — I’ll have the initial model by EOD Wednesday.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: John Park <john@velox.ai>

Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment mode qualification & next steps

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Concurrency: typical daytime peak ~120 RPS, occasional spikes to ~350 RPS for 10-15 minute windows.
- Embeddings: mostly async batch jobs (nightly), not latency-sensitive.
- Data: all PII redaction happens client-side; we still need SOC 2 + audit log retention for 1 year.
- Budget: we’re tracking to a ~USD $30k/month spend initially, but open to committing if the economics are clear.

What we’re looking for in your model:
1) Hosted per-token example (per 1M tokens) and predicted 95p latency at our peak.
2) Dedicated reserved pricing example (monthly commit + expected delivered RPS and cost per active token).
3) Private/VPC rough delta (one-time onboarding + recurring infra uplift).

If you can send a short comparison and recommended path, that’ll help us decide whether to pilot on Hosted or move to Dedicated commit.

—John
John Park
Head of ML Engineering | Velox AI
john@velox.ai

Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment mode qualification & next steps

John — thanks for the details. Attached is a concise pricing comparison (PDF) + a short modeling note below. I’ve kept assumptions conservative; if you update the workbook I’ll refresh the numbers.

Assumptions used (conservative)
- Avg tokens per req (prompt+response): 250 tokens
- Monthly requests: 10M -> ~2.5B tokens/month
- Peak sustained RPS for sizing: 350 (15 minute spikes)

High-level cost examples (monthly)
- Hosted API (pay-as-you-go per-token):
  - Model cost: $0.0006 / token (inference heavy model) -> ~ $1,500,000 / month (note: this is an upper bound; we can propose smaller/optimized model variants).
  - Expected 95p latency: likely ~150–250ms dependent on shared capacity; recommend Reserved Burst add-on to protect spikes.

- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools):
  - Example commit: $60k/month reserved capacity (N GPUs sized to handle base 150 RPS) + burst pool for spikes.
  - Effective unit cost: depends on utilization; with 70% utilization this maps to ~ $0.00009–0.00015 / token.
  - Pros: predictable latency, better tail behavior and lower unit cost at scale.

- Private VPC / On-prem:
  - One-time onboarding & infra uplift: ~$120–200k (depending on integrations and KMS/HSM work).
  - Recurring infra ops: customer-managed; Redwood support/licensing typically $15k–30k/month for enterprise plan.

Recommendation and next steps
- Short pilot on Hosted API for 4–6 weeks with Reserved Burst to validate latency/traffic profile while we model Dedicated sizing.
- If utilization drives predictable throughput (and you’re above ~$25–30k/month sustained), move to Dedicated reserved commit to reduce unit cost.
- Private only if you require customer-managed networking/KMS or stricter contractual controls.

I’m copying Marissa (Dedicated sizing) and Neha (pricing approvals) — Marissa, can you validate the $60k/month example sizing for 350 RPS spikes? Neha, I’ll flag this for a pricing review if John is inclined to commit.

Attached: redwood_pricing_table.pdf (high-level comparison)

If this looks reasonable, John — can we lock a 30-min call Thursday 10am PT to walk through the attached and agree next step?

Best,
Aditya Rao
